records.quote: It was nothing of this earth, but a piece of the great outside; and as such dowered with outside properties and obedient to outside laws.

records.quote: And because Ammi recognized that colour, and knew that this last faint remnant must still lurk down there in the well, he has never been quite right since.

records.quote: there burst up from that doomed and accursed farm a gleamingly eruptive cataclysm of unnatural sparks and substance; blurring the glance of the few who saw it, and sending forth to the zenith a bombarding cloudburst of such coloured and fantastic fragments as our universe must needs disown.
records.paraphrase: The farm erupts in a cataclysmic burst of unnatural coloured substance shooting into the sky.

records.quote: Under the spectroscope both samples gave off an unknown spectrum, in which many of the baffling bands were precisely like those which the strange meteor had yielded in the previous year. records.quote: All the orchard trees blossomed forth in strange colours, and through the stony soil of the yard and adjacent pasturage there sprang up a bizarre growth which only a botanist could connect with the proper flora of the region.

records.quote: The swine began growing grey and brittle and falling to pieces before they died, and their eyes and muzzles developed singular alterations.
records.paraphrase: The livestock undergo grotesque physical changes, greying and disintegrating before death.

records.quote: Then without warning the hideous thing shot vertically up toward the sky like a rocket or meteor, leaving behind no trail and disappearing through a round and curiously regular hole in the clouds before any man could gasp or cry out.

records.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts the entity with everything known in nature, framing it as an alien colour from beyond.

candidates.description: An alien entity or force that arrives embedded in a meteorite: a 'colour' from beyond known Nature that obeys laws foreign to our cosmos. It settles in the Gardner farm's well, drains the life from vegetation, animals, and humans, transforms the land into a permanent grey blasted wasteland, and ultimately departs skyward while leaving a lingering remnant that slowly spreads.

novelty.rationale: The colour is explicitly framed as 'nothing of this earth,' obedient to laws foreign to our cosmos, and a colour outside the known spectrum. Its arrival permanently alters the storyworld, converting fertile land into an eternal grey desert and slowly spreading blight. This is a totalizing, world-altering difference from the implied empirical norm rather than a mere curiosity.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The story develops a coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural account through repeated laboratory investigation (spectroscopy, solvent tests, affinity for silicon, unknown spectral bands) and extrapolative biological/ecological consequences. Although framed as 'beyond Nature as we know it,' it is consistently treated as an immanent material entity ('would be called a gas') obeying an alternate, imaginary physics rather than a magical or deific agent. Some rhetoric edges toward the numinous, but the immanent, investigable framing dominates.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The narrator states outright that 'it all began with the meteorite,' and every subsequent event\u2014crop failure, livestock deaths, madness, the disappearances, the cataclysmic eruption, the blasted heath, and the framing reservoir plot\u2014flows from the colour. It determines the whole narrative logic rather than acting as an incidental device.

estrangement.rationale: Reader-facing contrast is established by insistently defining the colour against the known spectrum and against 'all Nature as we know it,' while storyworld consequences (spreading blight, permanent grey desert, drained life) and character reactions (Mrs. Gardner's aphasic raving, Ammi's permanent psychological damage) provide the estranging register. Character surprise is present but not required for qualification.

candidates.description: The physical meteorite fragment and its embedded coloured globule as an anomalous laboratory specimen exhibiting impossible material properties (non-volatile, resistant to all solvents, affinity for silicon, unknown spectrum, wasting away in air).

novelty.rationale: As an object the fragment behaves in ways foreign to terrestrial chemistry and physics, representing a genuine departure from the empirical norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The specimen is subjected to systematic, immanent scientific investigation with coherent (if anomalous) described behavior.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The fragment and globule are the vector/container for the colour, but as a standalone specimen they are an incidental device: the fragments and globule are destroyed early and the narrative logic is governed by the colour entity itself, not by the rock specimen. Treated independently, this candidate does not determine the overriding narrative logic.

estrangement.rationale: The specimen's inexplicable laboratory behavior supplies reader-facing contrast against normal chemistry, but its storyworld consequences are subsumed into the broader colour novum rather than standing alone.
